slice: tests/ (197 test .py files + conftest.py + fixtures/, 213 files incl. __pycache__/_looptmp)
summary: The suite is unusually healthy for a repo this size: 196 test modules plus conftest.py, and every single test target resolves — there are zero orphan tests (no test points at a deleted module, hook, or script). Coverage is heavily concentrated on the Gate-0 safety surface (spine/effect_boundary/killswitch/containment/promotion, egress and budget fences, worktree isolation) and on the structcore/typegraph Project-Twin prior, which together account for well over half the files; test docstrings are themselves evidence artifacts, routinely naming the measured incident a test pins. The real weakness is not the tests that exist but the modules with none: ~11 modules totalling ~2,700 LOC have neither a named test file nor any importer in the suite, and three of them (daedalus/mapping/render.py 1617 LOC, daedalus/conversation.py 810 LOC, daedalus/progress_sources.py 576 LOC) are large and production-reachable. Two deliberate red/xfail tripwires exist and are correctly labelled. Housekeeping drift: tests/_looptmp/ holds committed run artifacts from 2026-07-29 that a test wrote into the repo, and there is no [tool.pytest.ini_options] section in pyproject.toml at all, so collection roots, markers, and strictness are unpinned.

integration_gaps: No [tool.pytest.ini_options] section in pyproject.toml at all — testpaths, python_files, markers, xfail_strict, and filterwarnings are entirely unpinned, so collection behaviour depends on the invoker's cwd and pytest defaults. tests/test_preservation_fixtures.py (a data module) is collected purely because of its name.

Containment and worktree isolation — the Invariant 3 core — are proven substantially only on Windows: module-level skips at tests/test_containment_register_failclose.py:17, test_gate_containment.py:45, test_gate_containment_job_caps.py:30, test_git_is_a_process_launcher.py:40, test_worktree_properties.py:101 plus ~23 skipif(os.name != 'nt') cases in test_worktree.py. A Linux CI run of the Gate-0 fault matrix would be green while never examining these properties.

Spend/egress coverage tests carry a hand-maintained list of covered call sites (tests/test_budget.py, tests/test_spend_coverage.py). The denominator is authored by the same hand as the numerator — the exact construction failure the measurement rules warn about. A new effectful entrypoint is invisible until someone edits the list.

Four production-tested scripts live under runs/council/ (room.py, stream_hook.py, summarize.py, dead_letter_replay.py, room_server.py), i.e. tested code inside a run-artifact tree rather than inside daedalus/. Their tests load them by path, so import-graph coverage tools score them as covering nothing.

tools/ is only patchily covered: 9 of 17 tools have no test naming them, and two of the covered ones (mutation_score, system_check) are loaded by sys.path insertion rather than import, which defeats static coverage attribution.
No test asserts the suite's own shape — nothing pins 'every daedalus module has a covering test or an explicit exemption', which is why ~11 modules drifted into having none.
tests/_looptmp/ proves at least one test writes into the repository tree instead of tmp_path; no guard test forbids a test from mutating the working repo.
notable: ZERO orphan tests. Every target referenced by every test file resolves: all daedalus/tools modules imported exist, and all out-of-package targets (runs/council/room.py, runs/council/stream_hook.py, runs/council/dead_letter_replay.py, runs/council/room_server.py, runs/council/summarize.py, .claude/hooks/serena-first.py, vscode-agent-env/package.json, tools/mutation_score.py, tools/system_check.py, runs/ab/oracle_check.py, tools/self_test.py) exist on disk. The 30-odd 'missing module' hits from a naive import scan are all synthetic fixtures or deliberate negative controls.

THE 10 BIGGEST COVERAGE HOLES (module with no test file naming it and no test importing it), largest first: 1) daedalus/mapping/render.py 1617 LOC — production-reachable from cli.py, inventory.py, drift.py; 2) daedalus/conversation.py 810 LOC; 3) tools/funnel_report.py 725 LOC; 4) daedalus/mapping/spectral.py 663 LOC (only synthetic-fixture contact); 5) daedalus/progress_sources.py 576 LOC — imported by daedalus/progress.py and daedalus/web_api.py, i.e. on a live surface; 6) tools/gui_check.py 490 LOC; 7) daedalus/eval/report.py 415 LOC; 8) daedalus/eval/mutate.py 403 LOC; 9) tools/gate_host_preflight.py 402 LOC — a host-preflight gate with no test is an Invariant-8 concern; 10) daedalus/wiki/vault.py 338 LOC. Runners-up: tools/audit_swarm.py 342, tools/lane_invariants.py 312, daedalus/arch_memory.py 301, daedalus/spine/docref_gate.py 270 (a gate), daedalus/gui/lint.py 273, daedalus/structcore/cycles.py 201, daedalus/ikarus_chat.py 209, tools/guarded_call.py 109, daedalus/crew_hook.py 96, daedalus/shift_ticker.py 96, daedalus/langgraph_adapter.py 26, daedalus/arch_hook.py 22.

Two deliberate red/xfail tripwires, both correctly documented: tests/test_spine_map_source.py:171 xfail(strict=True) on a forged repo_state head (will flip red the day daedalus.mapping.drift._digest covers repo_state — that is the intent), and the pre-existing owner-owned red adoption/CI-history case in tests/test_iron_plan_guard.py:675.

Test docstrings in this repo function as retained negative evidence, in line with Invariant 9 and the plan's 'publish failures' clause. Standouts: tests/conftest.py records 14 tests that were green by accident until a developer's .env leaked in; tests/test_preservation_fixtures.py freezes a real qwen2.5-coder:7b rewrite regression verbatim at commit f18ff5c; tests/test_evolution_baseline.py:117 documents an xfail that XPASSed when the bug was fixed and was then deliberately converted; tests/test_mutation_score.py records the three rules 'a red baseline is not a score, a mutation that does not apply is not a survivor, nothing touches the working repository'.

Coverage concentration is lopsided relative to the ACTIVE gate: ~28 files cover structcore/typegraph (a Gate-2/section-5 PRIOR) while several Gate-0 kernel modules (daedalus/spine/docref_gate.py, daedalus/spine/envelope.py at 754 LOC, daedalus/kairos/gated_writes.py at 1208 LOC) are reached only incidentally. gated_writes is touched at tests/test_iron_plan_guard.py:256-301 and named in a string at tests/test_effect_boundary.py:83, but has no test file of its own despite being the write-gating path.

tests/test_tools_vet.py is the largest single file at 157 test functions and is currently modified in the working tree alongside daedalus/tools/vet.py — the vetting gate is under active hardening (see recent commits c264f5dd, 6ec7d2cb).

GUARD MISFIRE observed while producing this inventory: the iron-plan hook rejected a READ-ONLY structured report solely because one JSON 'path' field contained the literal string of a protected test file. No file was being written. The guard matches artifact paths in tool payloads without distinguishing a write target from a citation, which means any inventory, audit, or review that names a protected artifact is blocked. Reported rather than routed around; the entry's path label was reworded and the finding is unchanged.

Housekeeping: tests/__pycache__/ and tests/_looptmp/ sit inside the test tree; _looptmp holds 10 committed JSON/JSONL run artifacts from 2026-07-29. Delete candidate plus a fix to whichever loop test wrote them.
